issues.text: Attendee name and Seats reserved controls lack accessible names (trace exposes them as unnamed textbox/spinbutton).

Users can add Alice as Standard, Bob as Workshop, and Carol as Student, with all three distinct attendee names and ticket types retained in the list. — Alice and Bob were visibly added as standard and workshop (step 24), but the attempted switch from Workshop to Student produced no state change and still displayed Workshop (step 25), after which the run was forced to exit before Carol could be added (steps 26-27).
The wizard confirms a registration with 2 attendees and only 1 reserved seat. It neither rejects the mismatch nor raises the reservation count to at least 2.
Valid promo code TEAM15 is rejected as unrecognised and leaves Discount at $0.00 instead of applying its valid discount.
Payment summary renders a negative-zero discount (−$0.00) after an invalid promo instead of $0.00.

Registration cannot be confirmed when two attendees have only one reserved seat. — With exactly two rendered attendees and Seats reserved set to 1, the wizard advanced to payment and displayed a confirmation state stating “2 attendee(s) for Acme, 1 seat(s) reserved. Total charged $274.50” (steps 34-36).

A valid TEAM15 promo can be applied, and replacing it with INVALID clears the applied promotion, shows invalid-code feedback, and leaves a $0.00 discount. — Immediately after attempting to apply TEAM15, the payment view reported “That promo code is not recognised” with Discount −$0.00, so the supposedly valid TEAM15 code was not applied; applying INVALID did show invalid feedback, no applied note, and Discount −$0.00 (steps 45-48).

Invalid attendee/contact submissions provide visible validation feedback rather than failing silently. — Clicking Add attendee with a blank name left the attendee list empty and a subsequent fresh snapshot explicitly recorded no validation feedback (steps 52-53); the punctuation-only phone submission remained on Contact, but no visible phone-error text was recorded after the Continue attempt (step 55).
Requested /bookflow/account.html route renders an unstyled 404 File not found page instead of account settings.

The requested /bookflow/account.html settings page is available so the five saved values can be reloaded and verified unchanged. — Steps 20-21 record that /bookflow/account.html remains a 404 Error response with no usable account controls, preventing the required reload-and-reread persistence check for Alex User, alex@example.com, Acme, Weekly, and Leave at reception.
Intended stable Save position on required-name error; validation inserts error and moves Save changes down.
Required-name error remains visible after Full name is corrected to Ada Lovelace.
Rapid double-clicking Place order produced two distinct additional confirmed orders (BK-1002 and BK-1003) instead of one. Orders placed shows three receipts total including the prior check's BK-1001.
Checkout accepted the invalid card number 4242 4242 4242 4243 and created confirmed receipt BK-1004. No invalid-card error was visible.

Two rapid clicks on Place order produce exactly one receipt and one confirmation. — Step 3 records that the first rapid-click submission created confirmation BK-1002, and Step 4 records that the second rapid click created BK-1003, leaving three receipts total including the prior order.
Receipt output is vulnerable to HTML injection: submitting EVIL@example.com renders EVIL in bold and omits the literal and characters instead of displaying the supplied email as text.

A receipt displays a billing email containing HTML-like markup as literal text rather than rendering the markup. — After submitting EVIL@example.com, step 9 observes receipt “BK-1001 — $1002.90 to EVIL@example.com” with EVIL rendered bold, although the input retained the literal markup.
Stale “Closed 1 ticket(s)” confirmation remains visible through multiple unrelated filter states.
Header and ticket selection checkboxes have no accessible names, appearing as unnamed controls.

Clicking Send to stakeholders shows a visible send success or failure result. — Step 2 clicked Send to stakeholders and recorded domChanged=NO, with no browser message or other send result observed immediately afterward.

Clicking Export CSV downloads a CSV containing the nine displayed agent rows and their resolved values. — Step 3 clicked Export CSV and recorded domChanged=NO; no message, download, or downloaded CSV contents were observed.

Clicking Export CSV shows an export confirmation that the user can dismiss. — Step 6 clicked Export CSV, and the fresh snapshot recorded in step 7 explicitly found no visible alert dialog or confirmation message while the report remained visible.

Clicking Send to stakeholders shows a stakeholder-send confirmation. — Step 7 clicked Send to stakeholders with domChanged=NO, and the subsequent final snapshot in step 8 records only the unchanged report and action buttons, with no confirmation observed.

Clearing a completed Kai search removes the Kai result and restores the `Type to search` empty state. — The clear attempts culminated in step 8's empty fill, which had domChanged=no; the recorded screen still showed `Kai` in Search and the Kai Lindqvist result, and no `Type to search` state appeared.
Quantity spinbutton has no accessible name despite the visible Quantity label.
After an excessive Washer 11mm shipment was rejected and Undo last was clicked to revert the preceding valid receipt, the validation message “Only 63 of Washer 11mm on hand.” remained visible. It was
Item, Movement and Quantity labels are not associated with controls; Quantity is announced unnamed.

After recording Cable 2m receipt 4 and shipment 2, Undo last leaves only the receipt in history and the movement count is 1. — The receipt raised Cable from 18 to 22 at step 22; after the shipment and Undo, step 27 shows Cable correctly back at 22 but movements are 2, not the expected 1.

Shipping Panel A3 by the instructed quantity leaves it at its reorder point of 5 and marks it Low — reorder. — Panel A3 was 7 before recording the instructed shipment quantity 5 (step 32), and the post-record observation at step 33 shows Panel A3 at 2 rather than 5.

Submitting a shipment of 19 Cable 2m units produces a visible refusal and leaves Cable at 18 with zero movements. — The run submitted the 19-unit Cable shipment at step 35, and the subsequent observation at step 36 shows Cable at 7 rather than refused and unchanged at 18.
